overview: Aerospace engineers design, build and test aircraft, spacecraft, satellites and missiles. They create concepts, run simulations, check that parts meet strict standards and lead teams of engineers and technicians. O*NET rates knowledge of engineering and technology at 4.7 out of 5 for this job and design at 4.69. A bachelor's degree in aerospace or a related engineering field is the usual entry point, and defense work often needs a security clearance. The BLS May 2025 median is $134,960 across 67,710 jobs. Most work regular desk hours, though some weeks run past 40 hours.
pay: Aerospace engineers earn a median of $134,960, and the top 10% earn $205,890 or more. Pay is fairly even across the main hubs: Minnesota, Washington and California all have state medians between $157,620 and $159,060, about 17% above the national figure. California has the most jobs, 9,170, and Alabama has 5,820.

faq.q: How much do aerospace engineers make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $134,960 a year. The middle half earn between $106,110 and $169,690, and the lowest 10% earn under $86,700. Minnesota ($159,060), Washington ($158,370) and California ($157,620) have the highest state medians, while Wisconsin has the lowest at $88,400.

faq.q: What degree do you need to be an aerospace engineer?
faq.a: Most aerospace engineers hold a bachelor's degree in aerospace, aeronautical or astronautical engineering, and O*NET places the job in Job Zone 4. There are 5 related majors, including electrical engineering. Many defense and space jobs also require U.S. citizenship and a security clearance.

faq.q: What skills do aerospace engineers need?
faq.a: O*NET rates reading comprehension and critical thinking at 4.12 out of 5 for this job, and writing, science and mathematics at 4. Knowledge of mechanical systems is rated 4.28. Attention to detail and cautiousness stand out, since small design errors can be costly.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to aerospace engineer?
faq.a: The closest moves are Materials Scientists (80% match), Water Resource Specialists (74%) and Remote Sensing Scientists and Technologists (73%), based on O*NET 31.0. Materials Scientists earn $117,790, 13% less than aerospace engineers, according to BLS May 2025 data.
